The Prophet told people to offer some of their prayers at home and not to make their houses like graves.
Aisha said the Prophet never missed two rak'at after Asr, praying them at home rather than in the mosque lest it burden his followers, and two before Fajr.
A prayer may be offered between adhan and iqama; companions prayed two rak'at before Maghrib, and the Prophet two light ones before Fajr, then lay on his right side.
The Prophet prayed two rak'at before and after Zuhr and after Maghrib and Isha, and after Jumua prayed two rak'at only once he was home.
On journeys the Prophet prayed voluntary prayers and witr on his mount, nodding, facing wherever it went, but dismounted and faced the Qibla for the compulsory prayers.
On journeys the Prophet prayed two rak'at and no optional prayers, yet Um Hani saw him pray eight rak'at of Duha, and he prayed nawafil on his mount at night.
The Prophet never missed the two light rak'at before Fajr, praying them after the adhan, then lay on his right side or talked with Aisha until the iqama.
The Prophet taught Istikhara's two rak'at and invocation and two rak'at on entering a mosque, even mid-sermon, and prayed two before and after Zuhr and after Jumua, Maghrib and Isha.
Ibn Umar doubted the Prophet prayed Duha and Aisha never saw it, yet Um Hani saw him pray eight rak'at, and he advised Abu Huraira to pray it.
The Prophet kept ten voluntary rak'at around the daily prayers, never missed four before Zuhr and two before Fajr, and allowed prayer before Maghrib without making it a tradition.
The Prophet prayed two rak'at at a spot Itban chose in his house, saying whoever declares Allah's oneness seeking His pleasure is saved from Hell; pray some prayers at home.
During the Anmar expedition the Prophet offers voluntary prayers on his mount, facing east.
The Prophet taught the Istikhara: two voluntary rak'at, then asking Allah by His knowledge and power to decree a matter if good and turn it away if bad.
The Prophet said thrice to pray before Maghrib, adding the third time that whoever wants may do so, lest people take it as a Sunna.
The Prophet taught the istikhara: two voluntary rak'at, then asking Allah, who knows and is able, to ease a matter if good and turn it away if not.
